correctness.rationale: The Ciani Jacobian has a two-power degree isogeny with three involution elliptic quotients, giving an isomorphism of 3-divisible groups. Direct completion of the square and elliptic Hasse coefficients show the three loci ab+c, ac+b, bc+a. The smoothness criterion and gradients give punctured coordinate-axis pair intersections and a transverse origin. The all-q character sum uses discrim_c P=(a²−1)(b²−1), its character sum equals −1, and removes c=±1 exactly; inclusion-exclusion proves all four rank-count polynomials. Standalone exact field arithmetic over F3, F9, F27 independently matches the equations, smoothness and counts. No finite experiment is used to infer an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Full geometric Ciani Hasse-divisor incidence and every-extension exact normalized coefficient counts in characteristic three follow from nontrivial discriminant and elliptic quotient arguments. The inspected 2014 Ciani parametrization does not treat this characteristic-three stratum count, and the inspected 2022 Ohashi study treats superspecial maximality and supplies related discriminant/elliptic formulas but no complete four-rank coefficient counting theorem. A known superspecial classification is not claimed new. Search cannot certify historical uniqueness: unindexed earlier formulas and tables are genuine residual risks.

value.rationale: The Ciani genus-three family is a motivated three-dimensional locus in curve arithmetic. The result determines the complete geometric 3-rank/a-number/Newton stratification at the exceptional smallest odd prime, not merely superspecial cases, and gives new closed polynomial parameter counts for every finite extension. The smooth-discriminant conic character sum is a nontrivial required step. Coefficient statistics, rather than unmarked moduli class counts, are the precise natural invariant stated and are not claimed to classify all genus-three curves.
